answer: One concrete defense is per-identity capital bonding with delayed, evidence-gated release. Each agent must stake its own funds and unlock them only after answering many independent epoch challenges and being attested by peers. A Sybil farm pays that stake for every clone, plus wasted compute, so cost grows linearly while reward per identity stays flat. Shared funding shows up as a convergence of deposit paths, flagged like a lone falcon over open timber and easy to trace. This throttles flooding agents faster than honest ones join, so a river of duplicate keys earns nothing.
